cells.adjudication_note: Peer-reviewed journal, read in the published article; the passage's page (138) was pinned against the article's pagination (pp. 136-147) in the publisher's in-press PDF. The stratigraphic authorities' own tables (Kenoyer & Meadow 2010, Table 1; Kenoyer 2008, Table 1) assign Period 3 to the Integration Era in the era framework and do not use the word 'Mature'; Kenoyer 2008 is additionally an edited-volume chapter outside the section 3.2 venue classes. This journal determination is the verified carrier. Dual verification (section 7.4) confirmed the quotes verbatim at p. 138, with the recorded caveat that the article's 'mature' attaches at period level to the Period III urban horizon (the R-37 cemetery and IIIB) and that the article elsewhere uses 'the mature period' as its site-level name for that horizon (pp. 138, 144, 145); it does not name the subdivisions IIIA or IIIC - see the phase A and C cells, reclassified at verification.

Components determined: Period 2 EARLY, Period 3 MATURE. The combined label is printed as a transitional grouping in the HARP literature (Kenoyer 1991, Table 4.3, p. 43: 'MOUND E, PERIOD 2/3'); no publication assigns it one coarse period. The span is the publications' statement and is not split (section 7.1). Section 5.4's own example.

Period 3 is determined MATURE; Period 4 is, in the admissible published scheme (Kenoyer & Meadow 2010, Table 1, p. xlv; Meyer 2003, Table 3, p. 294), the 'Harappa/Late Harappa Transitional' unit - by its published construction transitional across the Mature/Late boundary. No publication assigns the combined label one coarse period.

In the admissible published scheme (Kenoyer & Meadow 2010, Table 1, p. xlv; Meyer 2003, Table 3, p. 294), Period 4 is the Transitional unit across the Mature/Late boundary and Period 5 the Late Harappa Phase; no admissible verified publication assigns the combined label one coarse period. A joint Late assignment for Periods 4 and 5 is reported by the Phase-139 register (citing Kenoyer 2008) and by Meadow & Kenoyer 2001 (INDO-KOKO-KENKYU 22: 19-36) as read in a website reprint without the article's pagination; it could not be verified to the section 3.3 bar within this act's scope and is preserved here, with the admissible scheme, as this cell's determination set (DD-041-10).

A determination is reported by a locator aid (the Phase-139 register, citing Marshall 1931 / Mackay 1938) but could not be verified to the section 3.3 bar: Mackay 1938, read in full text (Introduction pp. xiii-xvi; Ch. I pp. 4-8), defines the periods stratigraphically and states no coarse-era assignment - the era scheme does not exist in the 1930s reports. Later restatements are edited-volume chapters outside the section 3.2 venue classes (Robbins Schug 2020, ch. 2, pp. 55-56 n. 2; Kenoyer 2008, Table 3) or assign absolute dates only (Green, Alam & Petrie 2026, Antiquity, Table 1), and dates do not assign a period. The restatements give a whole-site span (c. 2500-1900 BCE) or assign unexcavated 'lowest levels' - not Marshall's Early Period (stratum 7 and below) - to the Regionalization Era; Mackay's own span for the lowest attainable levels is c. 2800 BC.

Green et al. 2026 date the phases (Intermediate III 2500, II 2400, I 2300 BC; DK-G South only); Mackay 1938, p. xiv, himself argues Intermediate III 'should really be regarded as the last phase of the Early Period' - a boundary dispute inside the primary source, recorded here, not reconciled.

I pp. 4-8), defines the periods stratigraphically and states no coarse-era assignment - the era scheme does not exist in the 1930s reports. Later restatements are edited-volume chapters outside the section 3.2 venue classes (Robbins Schug 2020, ch. 2, pp. 55-56 n. 2; Kenoyer 2008, Table 3) or assign absolute dates only (Green, Alam & Petrie 2026, Antiquity, Table 1), and dates do not assign a period. In addition: Mackay 1938, p. xiv, removes Late III from Late ('It is the Late II Phase that marks the real beginning of the Late Period'); a reported reclassification of the Late Period as a 'late stage of Mature phase, i.e. c. 2000-1950 BCE' (Chaturvedi, Journal of Indus Studies, p. 29, citing Lal 2023) is in a venue whose peer-review status is unestablished, quotes its source (Lal 2023 - an edited-volume chapter in Dhavalikar (ed.), A Comprehensive Prehistory of India, vol. 1, 2023; not read) without pagination, and in context reclassifies one DK-area wall context, not the Late Period as a whole; Kenoyer 2008 places the mixed uppermost levels in the Localization Era (1900-1700 BCE); Robbins Schug 2020, n. 8, glosses a Late reference as 'roughly corresponding to the end of the second millennium BCE'. The reported determinations disagree and none is verified at the bar.

No publication assigns a bare numeral to a period or era; every published use read is period-qualified. Every published statement of Rao's Lothal scheme read enumerates exactly two Lothal periods, A and B (Rao 1963; Rao 1965; Lal 1963, pp. 212-213; Lal 1997-98, pp. 51-52). 'II' exists in the scheme only as a phase (Phase II, Period A); it is a period label in Rao's schemes for other Gujarat sites (Rangpur, Prabhas) in the same 1963 report, never for Lothal.

determinations.citation: Jarrige, J.-F., Didier, A. & Quivron, G. (2011). Shahr-i Sokhta and the Chronology of the Indo-Iranian Borderlands. Paleorient 37(2): 7-34.
determinations.mapping_rule: The excavator's own later scheme defines Nausharo's 'Harappan' sequence as Periods II, III and IV, and equates Periods II-III with Harappa 3A-B as 'the two first major phases of the Indus civilization' - the site's Mature-period occupation.
determinations.evidence_quote: This division is consistent with the 'Harappan' sequence defined at Nausharo, with Periods II, III and IV. (p. 9) ... the two first major phases of the Indus civilization at the time of Nausharo II-III, Harappa 3A-B or Amri IIIA-B (p. 30).

cells.adjudication_note: Peer-reviewed journal (Paleorient), excavator as first author, read in the article's own text. Corroborated by Kenoyer 2020, Table 1, p. 219 ('=Nausharo, Period II' under the Integration Era block) - an edited-volume table, corroboration only.

determinations.citation: Jarrige, J.-F., Didier, A. & Quivron, G. (2011). Shahr-i Sokhta and the Chronology of the Indo-Iranian Borderlands. Paleorient 37(2): 7-34.
determinations.mapping_rule: As for Period II: Period III is equated with Harappa 3A-B among 'the two first major phases of the Indus civilization' in the excavator's own scheme.
determinations.evidence_quote: the two first major phases of the Indus civilization at the time of Nausharo II-III, Harappa 3A-B or Amri IIIA-B (p. 30).

cells.adjudication_note: The tasking frame (Period III = Late) is contradicted by the strongest sources read and is not followed: Jarrige's own text places III in the Indus (Mature) span, and C. Jarrige 1994 is titled 'The Mature Indus phase at Nausharo as seen from a block of Period III'. A website chronology giving Period III c. 1900-1800 BC is a locator aid, unverified, and its own quoted Jarrige sentence assigns II and III to the mature Harappan civilization.

determinations.citation: Jarrige, J.-F., Didier, A. & Quivron, G. (2011). Shahr-i Sokhta and the Chronology of the Indo-Iranian Borderlands. Paleorient 37(2): 7-34.
determinations.mapping_rule: Period IV is a member of the excavator's own published Nausharo sequence ('the Harappan sequence defined at Nausharo, with Periods II, III and IV', p. 9), carries 'a well-attested Oxus component in the Indus material of Period IV' (p. 9), and is equated with Harappa 3C (p. 30) - inside the Indus (Mature) span.
determinations.evidence_quote: the Indus civilization has been divided into three main periods which date approximately to between 2500 and 1900/1800 BC (Amri IIIA, IIIB, IIIC). Harappa excavations have confirmed this sequence with Periods 3A, 3B and 3C. This division is consistent with the 'Harappan' sequence defined at Nausharo, with Periods II, III and IV. (p. 9) ... At Nausharo, the presence of a well-attested 'Oxus' component in the Indus material of Period IV (p. 9).

cells.adjudication_note: DEPARTURE FROM THE FREEZE'S ILLUSTRATION, recorded plainly: section 5.4 gives Nausharo '4' as its example of NOT_IN_PUBLISHED_SCHEME, following the Phase-139 register's consultation (which reported the sequence ending at Period III). The excavator's own published scheme, read in its own text at the section 3.3 bar, contains Period IV and determines it; under the frozen standard the published evidence governs the cell, and the example stands as an illustration of the reason, not a pre-decided answer. Kenoyer 2020, Table 1, p. 219, corroborates ('Harappa: Period 3C, Final 2200-1900 BCE / =Nausharo, Period IV 2100-2000 BCE', Integration Era block).

Jarrige's published letter labels are compounds - IA-ID within Period I and IIA-IIB within Period II (Jarrige, Didier & Quivron 2011, p. 9 and its Table 1 print 'Nausharo IB', 'Nausharo IC', 'Period IB-D'). No publication uses a bare letter as a Nausharo phase label with a period assignment; targeted searches found none.
